findings.title: Fallback locales are only loaded on the web-request path
findings.description:
`set_locale` is the only caller of `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`. A search for `ensure_loaded` finds no other callers. Other paths that set a non-default locale never load the fallback locale: `app/services/post_alerter.rb:138` (`I18n.with_locale(user.effective_locale)`), `lib/post_destroyer.rb:102`, and `app/jobs/base.rb:151`. The freedom patch's `translate` loads only `config.locale` (`lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:68`). So in a Sidekiq process that has not served a request, `:en` is never loaded and the fallback silently finds nothing.

It is worse than a missing fallback. `translate` caches results under a key built from the current locale only (`translate_accelerator.rb:71-76`). If a non-English key misses before `:en` is loaded, the "translation missing" string is cached. It survives the later `ensure_loaded!` call until `I18n.reload!`. The eager load should happen where the cache key is computed, or inside `translate`, rather than depending on each entry point to remember the call.

findings.title: No spec covers the fallback chain or `ensure_loaded!`
findings.description: A search of `spec/` for `fallback`, `ensure_loaded`, and `FallbackLocaleList` returns nothing relevant. The only `set_locale` specs (`spec/controllers/application_controller_spec.rb:88-108`) assert `I18n.locale` and never check that a missing key resolves to the English string or that `:en` is loaded. Add a spec for a non-English locale with a key missing in that locale, and one for the site-default fallback step.

findings.title: An unguarded SiteSetting read now sits inside every fallback-enabled lookup
findings.description: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` calls `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` with no guard. That is a DB-backed read. The Fallbacks backend consults `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` on each lookup, so every `I18n.t` now performs that read and allocates an array. The codebase already treats this read as fallible: `lib/tasks/db.rake:3` and `:28` wrap the same call in `rescue :en`. The new code has no equivalent guard, so an early-boot or pre-migration translation can raise from inside I18n. Wrap the read in the same rescue, or cache the default and refresh it from the site-setting change hook.

findings.title: `set_locale` depends on a duck-typed method that the stock fallbacks object lacks
findings.description: `set_locale` calls `ensure_loaded!` on whatever `I18n.fallbacks` currently is. Only `FallbackLocaleList` defines it; the stock `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks` does not. Removing `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` from `production.rb`, `profile.rb`, and the cloud66 file is what makes this safe today. If someone re-adds that line, Rails' i18n railtie should replace the list with the stock object (I believe this from Rails 4.x behavior; I did not verify it here). Every request would then raise `NoMethodError` in `set_locale`, and nothing guards or tests for that. Make the contract explicit, or add a comment or spec that forbids re-adding the config line.

findings.title: `FallbackLocaleList` has design issues
findings.description: The class subclasses `Hash` but never uses Hash storage; it only overrides `[]`. A plain class would state the intent. Two smaller issues: `.compact` on line 17 can never remove anything, because `.to_sym` on nil would already have raised. And `.uniq` does not dedupe mixed types. The call at `app/mailers/user_notifications.rb:48` passes `locale: 'en'` as a String, so the list becomes `['en', :en]` and English is tried twice. The top-level constant could also live under a namespace.

findings.title: Fallbacks now apply in dev and test, not only in production
findings.description: The fallback config was previously set only in `production.rb` and `profile.rb`. The initializer runs in every environment, so development and test now quietly show English and the site default when a non-English key is missing. The integrity checks in `spec/integrity/i18n_spec.rb` run in `:en`, so they are unaffected. If the dev/test change is intended, say so in a comment or the commit message. If not, gate the initializer to production.

findings.title: New `ensure_loaded!` is undocumented and inconsistent with `translate`
findings.description: `ensure_loaded!` is a new public method on `I18n` with no comment. The file header (lines 1-9) still describes only on-demand loading, so it does not say that fallback locales now need an explicit call. The method uses `@loaded_locales ||= []`, while `translate` at line 68 uses a bare `include?`, so the two handle nil state differently. Add a doc comment on when to call it and why, and make the nil handling consistent.

findings.title: Config removal is complete and the pluralization move preserves behavior
findings.description: A repo-wide search finds no remaining `config.i18n.fallbacks` setting in any environment or cloud file, so the removal is complete with no double configuration. The `Pluralization` include on `I18n::Backend::Simple` still runs after `02-freedom_patches.rb`, so moving it from `pluralization.rb` into `i18n.rb` does not change behavior.
